scope: Batch addition of aliases on the entity types supported by Apollo, for an editor permitted to edit those aliases.
summary: Apollo covers the important batch-add fields and also edits and removes existing aliases. This is the strongest replacement candidate in the pilot.

capabilities.name: Add several aliases with a shared edit note
capabilities.reason: Both implementations submit one edit per alias; Apollo provides multiple new rows.

capabilities.name: Name, sort name, type, locale and primary flag
capabilities.reason: Apollo reads available types/locales from MusicBrainz and sends each of these fields.

capabilities.name: Inspect individual submission results
capabilities.reason: Both retain per-row success or failure feedback.

gaps: No important gap found in the inspected batch-add implementation. This is code-level coverage, not a live submission comparison.

migration: Open an entity's Aliases or Add alias page with Apollo's bulk alias editor enabled. Enter the rows and review before submitting. Disable the other alias editor during the check.

scope: Remembering and recalling submitted MusicBrainz edit notes; AcoustID and automatic last-note prefilling are outside the covered route.
summary: Mammoth provides submitted-note history and reusable notes on MusicBrainz, but Elephant also runs on AcoustID and automatically inserts the last note into empty forms.

capabilities.name: Remember and recall submitted notes
capabilities.reason: Elephant keeps ten memories; Mammoth records deduplicated history and supports saved notes.

capabilities.name: Automatically prefill an empty note with the last note
capabilities.reason: Elephant explicitly calls forceValue for the last note on load; no matching default note-prefill behavior found in Mammoth.

capabilities.name: Note memory on AcoustID edit pages
capabilities.reason: Elephant matches acoustid.org/edit/*; Mammoth's match is MusicBrainz.

gaps: Keep Elephant for AcoustID note memory or its automatic last-note prefilling.
The wiki description mentions dates, but this captured Elephant entry script implements note memory; do not infer date handling from that description.
Stored notes are not automatically migrated from Elephant's localStorage to Mammoth's GM storage.
migration: Copy important notes into Mammoth's Import / Export tab and compare recall behavior on MusicBrainz. Keep Elephant where its uncovered workflows matter.

scope: Importing ordinary public Bandcamp digital albums; archived/private pages and download/stream availability rules are material differences.
summary: First Contact seeds the main release data and Apollo handles matching. The dedicated importer has additional Bandcamp-specific behavior that prevents a general uninstall recommendation.

capabilities.name: Seed title, artists, tracks, lengths, date, barcode and notes
capabilities.reason: Both have Bandcamp data readers and release seeding; exact output and date/artist heuristics can differ.

capabilities.name: Download/free-stream links and hidden download tracks
capabilities.reason: The dedicated importer distinguishes free downloads and hidden track counts. First Contact's inspected reader seeds purchase and conditional streaming URLs without that full decision tree.

capabilities.name: Import from archived pages and private-stream handling
capabilities.reason: The dedicated importer matches Wayback and has private-stream status/link handling; First Contact matches live album/track pages.

gaps: Archived Bandcamp pages, private streams and hidden download tracks need the dedicated importer or manual handling.
Do not assume identical free-download, streaming, release-date or artist-credit results.
First Contact saves imported pages to the Internet Archive by default; turn that setting off if unwanted.
migration: For a public digital album, use First Contact and review the seeded metadata in Apollo. Compare source-specific URLs and hidden tracks before disabling the dedicated importer.
